questions.question: A pipeline reports 97% overall extraction accuracy. Why is this number alone dangerous for deciding whether to automate?
options: It's a volume-weighted average that can hide a low-accuracy, low-volume segment behind a high-accuracy, high-volume one
It's always calculated incorrectly by most pipelines
It only reflects schema validation, never semantic validation
97% is too high to be realistic, so the number is probably fabricated

questions.question: What is the recommended fix before trusting an aggregate accuracy number enough to act on it?
options: Round it down by a safety margin before using it
Break it down by document type, by field, and by the cross of both
Re-run the same eval set three times and average the results
Ignore it and rely only on confidence calibration

questions.question: A pipeline automates a 99.5%-accurate invoice segment while routing 100% of a 60%-accurate scanned-receipt segment to humans, but reports a single 97% blended figure. What's the problem with that reported number?
options: There is no problem, blending is standard practice
It papers over a gating decision that should be reflected per-segment, not as one figure
60% accuracy is impossible for any document type
The math must be wrong since 97% doesn't match a simple average

questions.question: What statistical phenomenon is the aggregate-metrics trap most closely related to?
options: The central limit theorem
Simpson's-paradox-adjacent aggregation across heterogeneous subgroups
Survivorship bias in hiring data
Regression to the mean

questions.question: Why can segment-level accuracy numbers themselves be misleading if taken at face value?
options: Segments with small sample sizes can swing wildly (e.g. 60% to 90%) on a single extra correct/incorrect case
Segment-level numbers are never comparable across document types
Segmentation always increases the reported accuracy artificially
Segments can't be defined for structured data pipelines

questions.question: The aggregate-metrics trap principle applies to which stages of the extraction pipeline lifecycle?
options: Only the initial extraction step
Only production monitoring, not calibration or review allocation
Any stage that produces an accuracy number used to gate a decision — calibration, review sizing, and drift monitoring alike
Only semantic validation, since schema validation isn't measured in accuracy terms
